segments.t: In his dressing room after an emotional day of filming, Herve chats with makeup artist Vero. Impressed by his natural acting talent, Vero shares an exciting rumor she overheard from the film director. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Hervé, je suis très occupée aujourd'hui.
Tout est prêt dans ta loge.
Bien sûr Véro, pas de souci.
Tu étais encore extraordinaire sur le plateau!
Merci, c'était vraiment très intense.
Mais le tournage passe tellement vite.
Je veux encore profiter de ça.
Écoute, j'ai un grand secret.
Ta carrière d'acteur continue peut-être!
Quoi? Qu'est-ce que tu dis?
Valérie pense à toi maintenant.
Elle prépare son prochain grand film.
Elle veut te donner un vrai rôle!
C'est le plus beau jour!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Hervé, je suis très occupée aujourd'hui.
'Herve, I am very busy today.' Vero pops into the room while juggling several tasks on set. The descriptive adjective for 'busy' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Tout est prêt dans ta loge.
'Everything is ready in your dressing room.' She lets him know that the makeup remover is laid out. The informal 'you' form around 'dressing room' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Bien sûr Véro, pas de souci.
'Of course Vero, no problem.' Herve is happy to remove his own makeup without fuss. The descriptive adjective for 'sure' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Tu étais encore extraordinaire sur le plateau!
'You were amazing again on the set!' Vero compliments his moving performance in front of the crew. The verb meaning 'were' pairs naturally with the noun for 'set' in everyday conversation.
Merci, c'était vraiment très intense.
'Thank you, it was truly very intense.' Herve is still emotional from acting out the dramatic scene. The descriptive adjective for 'intense' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Mais le tournage passe tellement vite.
'But the shoot goes by so fast.' Herve wishes his time as an actor did not end so quickly. Notice how 'goes by' leads directly into the noun meaning 'shoot'.
Je veux encore profiter de ça.
'I still want to enjoy this.' He wants to savor every moment on set before returning to agency desk work. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'want'.
Écoute, j'ai un grand secret.
'Listen, I have a big secret.' Vero lowers her voice to share confidential gossip from the crew. The descriptive adjective for 'big' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Ta carrière d'acteur continue peut-être!
'Your acting career continues perhaps!' Vero hints that this small part might lead to more roles. The verb meaning 'continues' pairs naturally with the noun for 'career' in everyday conversation.
Quoi? Qu'est-ce que tu dis?
'What? What are you saying?' The informal 'you' form around 'say' marks a direct, personal relationship. The informal 'you' form around 'say' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Valérie pense à toi maintenant.
'Valerie is thinking of you now.' Vero reveals that the film director was praising Herve earlier. Vero uses the casual singular 'you' with 'thinks', showing close familiarity.
Elle prépare son prochain grand film.
'She is preparing her next big film.' The director is already planning her upcoming feature project. The verb meaning 'prepares' pairs naturally with the noun for 'movie' in everyday conversation.
Elle veut te donner un vrai rôle!

'She wants to give you a real role!' Vero adds that the director has a major part in mind for him. The reflexive pronoun sits right in front of the verb for 'wants', turning the action back onto the subject.
C'est le plus beau jour!

'It is the most beautiful day!' Herve beams with joy at the prospect of becoming a real movie star. The key noun here means 'day', anchored by its matching French article. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.
